proof:
Source: Steps 0 and 3 of the supplied parent proof. Step 0 localises μ to open subsets of U of finite measure; Step 3 applies outer regularity of the finite restricted measures to obtain a small open neighbourhood. Here the compact exhaustion K_p, W_p := interior K_{p+1} is replaced by an equivalent countable cover of U by open balls of finite μ-measure, and the per-ball neighbourhoods are glued with a summable budget. This gives one open set for all of Z, so the parent needs no index p. Only facts inside the import closure of GMT.Ch08.Submission are used. Euclidean N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) is a proper, second-countable metric space whose σ-algebra is the Borel σ-algebra.

1. Local radii. Let x ∈ U. Since U is open there is ε > 0 with ball x ε ⊆ U (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put r_x := ε/2 > 0. Then closedBall x r_x ⊆ ball x ε ⊆ U (closedBall_subset_ball, as ε/2 < ε). By choice, fix such an r_x > 0 with closedBall x r_x ⊆ U for every x ∈ U; the value off U is irrelevant.

2. Finite-measure balls. For x ∈ U put W_x := ball x r_x. It is open, x ∈ W_x because r_x > 0, and W_x ⊆ closedBall x r_x ⊆ U. The closed ball is compact (isCompact_closedBall; Euclidean N is proper) and contained in U, so μ(closedBall x r_x) ≠ ∞ by hypothesis. Hence μ(W_x) ≤ μ(closedBall x r_x) < ∞.

3. Countable subcover (Lindelöf). We have ⋃_{x∈U} W_x = U: the inclusion ⊆ holds by Step 2, and ⊇ holds because x ∈ W_x. Euclidean N is second countable, so Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_biUnion_countable (Topology/Bases.lean:942), applied to the family of open sets (W_x)_{x∈U}, gives a countable T ⊆ U with ⋃_{x∈T} W_x = ⋃_{x∈U} W_x = U.

4. Budget. Since ζ > 0 we have ζ ≠ 0, and T (as a type) is countable. ENNReal.exists_pos_sum_of_countable (Analysis/SpecificLimits/Basic.lean:642) gives ε : T → ℝ≥0 with ε_i > 0 for every i ∈ T and Σ'_{i∈T} ε_i < ζ, the sum taken in ℝ≥0∞.

5. Outer regularity on one ball. Fix i ∈ T, so i ∈ U, and let ν_i := μ.restrict W_i.
- ν_i(univ) = μ(W_i) < ∞ by Step 2, so ν_i is a finite measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict) on the metric space Euclidean N with its Borel σ-algebra.
- Hence ν_i is weakly regular (Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure, MeasureTheory/Measure/Regular.lean:1072), and in particular outer regular.
- W_i is open, hence measurable. So for the arbitrary set Z, ν_i(Z) = μ(Z ∩ W_i) ≤ μ(Z) = 0 < ε_i (Measure.restrict_apply', which needs no measurability of Z, and measure_mono_null).
- By Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt (Regular.lean:359, valid for arbitrary sets under outer regularity) there is an open O'_i ⊇ Z with ν_i(O'_i) < ε_i.
- Since O'_i is open, hence measurable, μ(O'_i ∩ W_i) = ν_i(O'_i) < ε_i (Measure.restrict_apply).

6. Gluing. Put O := ⋃_{i∈T} (O'_i ∩ W_i).
(a) O is open, as a union of intersections of two open sets.
(b) O ⊆ ⋃_{i∈T} W_i ⊆ U by Step 2.
(c) Z ⊆ O. Let z ∈ Z. Then z ∈ U = ⋃_{i∈T} W_i by Step 3, so z ∈ W_i for some i ∈ T. Also z ∈ Z ⊆ O'_i by Step 5, hence z ∈ O'_i ∩ W_i ⊆ O.
(d) By countable subadditivity over the countable index type T (measure_iUnion_le) and Steps 5 and 4, μ(O) ≤ Σ'_{i∈T} μ(O'_i ∩ W_i) ≤ Σ'_{i∈T} ε_i < ζ.
This also covers the degenerate case U = ∅: then T = ∅, Z = ∅, O = ∅ and μ(O) = 0 < ζ. Hence O is open with Z ⊆ O ⊆ U and μ(O) < ζ. ∎
